basis: Herodotus records that the Scythians call Zeus 'Papaios'
Both are the sky-father at the head of the pantheon
Herodotus equates the Scythian Api with Ge, the Earth
Both are the earth as divine mother and consort of the sky-father
Herodotus equates Argimpasa with Aphrodite Ourania
Both are the heavenly goddess of love and sovereignty
Greek writers name the Egyptian Set as Typhon
Both are the storm-chaos rival who fights the reigning order and the rightful heir
Both are an ancient sky-sovereign who encompasses the world
A shared root for the two names has long been proposed
parallels.scholarly_caveat: The Varuna–Ouranos etymology is old and widely doubted; treat it as a possibility, not a finding.

basis: Desire personified as a god
In the Rigveda, desire (kama) is the first seed of mind at creation, as Eros is among the first powers in Hesiod
Spanish missionaries used 'Supay' to translate 'the Devil' in Quechua catechisms
Supay rules the inner world of the dead, the realm the missionaries equated with hell
parallels.scholarly_caveat: The equation is a missionary translation. In Andean tradition Supay is an ambivalent lord of the inner earth, not a principle of evil.

basis: Igbo Bible translations and preaching render 'Satan' as Ekwensu
Both are agents of disorder who lead people astray
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Before missionary use, Ekwensu was an ambivalent trickster and war power, not an evil adversary of God.

basis: Moravian and Danish missionaries in Greenland identified Tornarsuk with the Devil
Both stand at the head of the spirit powers outside the missionaries' God
parallels.scholarly_caveat: Tornarsuk was the master of the shamans' helping spirits; the devil reading is a missionary recasting.

basis: Jesuit missionaries named Yurupari as the Devil in Tupi-language teaching
In Northwest Amazonian tradition he is the culture-hero lawgiver of the sacred flutes
parallels.scholarly_caveat: A missionary demonization of a culture hero; the two roles are opposites.

basis: In Trinidad Orisha worship, Ogun is venerated through Saint Michael the Archangel
Both are the armed warrior who defends the faithful
Wiccan writings present the Horned God as the god known to the Greeks as Pan
Both are the horned lord of beasts and wild nature
parallels.syncretic_source: Gerald Gardner, Witchcraft Today (1954), and later Wiccan liturgy

basis: Lévi's goat-headed Baphomet draws on the horned, goat-footed image of Pan
Both are images of nature's generative force
parallels.syncretic_source: Éliphas Lévi, Dogme et Rituel de la Haute Magie (1854–56)

basis: The same morning-star god under the shared Semitic name ʿAthtar
Venus as a male divinity in both pantheons
